visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 accurately shows the projectile setup with a ground-level launch, 30° velocity vector, component labels, parabolic path, and vertical-motion equation tied to the range problem, whereas Lesson 1 is more generic and its mid-frame emphasizes 34.64 m/s with decorative arrows and a less clearly connected or positionally precise projectile diagram.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a clearly wired, well-formed fill-in gate after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, success message, and remediation path, while Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 is concise, naturally paced, and speaks the math cleanly, while Lesson 1 is clear but much more verbose and rhetorically inflated, which risks slower pacing and listener fatigue despite having no major pronunciation defects.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that mostly align with the narration’s references, while Lesson 1 has no beat/timing or cue data at all, making its visual-narration synchronization unverifiable and effectively much weaker on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly and explicitly walks through decomposition, vertical time of flight, and horizontal range with the needed numerical values, while Lesson 2 is mathematically aligned but skips the actual vertical-time calculation in the script and overgeneralizes the range formula without clearly stating its same-height/no-drag limitations.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is more visually polished with large legible text, a centered and consistent hand-drawn style, and cleaner composition, while Lesson 2’s mid-lesson layout is off-center with a tiny hard-to-read diagram, excessive empty space, low-contrast elements, and visible player UI clutter.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: four of six agents preferred it, with strong confidence in visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, and synchronization. Its projectile setup, timed cues, concise narration, and functional interaction gate were judged substantially stronger. Lesson 1 did win two important high-confidence dimensions—concept accuracy and polish—because it more explicitly walks through the full calculation and has cleaner visual composition. However, the weighted balance of the six verdicts favors Lesson 2 overall, despite its weaker mathematical completeness and visual polish.
